primary_region: Maharashtra — Jalgaon, Nandurbar, Dhule, Solapur belts

Healthy.visual_symptoms: Deep green, wide leaves without spots or tears. Pseudostem firm, no discolouration. Uniform bunch development.
immediate_actions: Regular drip irrigation
Balanced K and N fertilization
Healthy.timeline: G9 variety typically flowers at 8-9 months, harvest at 11-14 months.

Panama Wilt (Fusarium Wilt).causal_agent: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense Race 1 and Tropical Race 4 (TR4)
Panama Wilt (Fusarium Wilt).visual_symptoms: Older leaves yellow and collapse from base upward. Yellow to brown streaking inside pseudostem when cut. Internal vascular tissue shows red-brown discolouration. Plant wilts and dies. Distinctive 'yellowing ladder' — oldest leaves first.
Panama Wilt (Fusarium Wilt).favourable_conditions: Soil temperature 24-28°C, infected soil or planting material. Spreads through water movement, root contact, and contaminated tools. Race 4 affects G9.
Panama Wilt (Fusarium Wilt).severity_note: Most devastating banana disease globally. No effective chemical cure. Infected plants must be destroyed. Soil remains infested for 25+ years. Report suspected TR4 to agriculture department immediately.
immediate_actions: Mark infected plants and DO NOT remove — uproot and burn in place
Quarantine the affected area — prevent people, animals, tools leaving the zone
Disinfect all tools with bleach or formaldehyde solution
Do NOT irrigate from infected field water downstream
Report to Krishi Vigyan Kendra or district agriculture office
preventive_measures: Plant only certified disease-free tissue culture plants from reputed nurseries
Never bring planting material from farms with unknown disease history
Maintain farm hygiene — wash boots before entering fields
Avoid waterlogging — Panama Wilt spreads faster in wet soils
Use Pseudomonas fluorescens + Trichoderma bio-inoculants at planting
Keep soil pH 6.5-7.0 — extreme pH favours Fusarium
do_not: Move infected plant material, soil, or tools off-farm
Irrigate from fields where infection was detected
Plant banana on infected land without 5+ year break and soil treatment
Ignore early yellowing — by the time visible, often advanced
watch_for: Yellowing starting from oldest/outer leaves and progressing inward
Collapsed pseudostem with red-brown internal staining
Multiple plants affected in a row (indicates soil pathway spread)
Panama Wilt (Fusarium Wilt).timeline: Once visible, plant dies within 2-6 weeks. Adjacent plants may be infected but show no symptoms for months. Act immediately on detection.

Sigatoka (Yellow Sigatoka / Black Sigato.causal_agent: Yellow: Mycosphaerella musicola | Black: Mycosphaerella fijiensis
Sigatoka (Yellow Sigatoka / Black Sigato.visual_symptoms: Yellow Sigatoka: Light yellow streaks on leaves expanding to brown oval spots with yellow halo. Black Sigatoka: Black streaks with yellow halo, more aggressive. Severe infection causes premature leaf death, early ripening (shrivelled fingers).
Sigatoka (Yellow Sigatoka / Black Sigato.favourable_conditions: High humidity >90%, temperature 26-28°C, frequent rainfall. Worse in dense plantations with poor air circulation.
Sigatoka (Yellow Sigatoka / Black Sigato.severity_note: Can cause 30-50% yield loss. Black Sigatoka is more destructive than Yellow. G9 is moderately susceptible.
immediate_actions: Spray Mancozeb 0.2% or Propiconazole 0.1% immediately
Remove and destroy all severely affected leaves (do not leave in field)
Reduce canopy density — remove excess suckers
Spray mineral oil 1-2% (blocks spore germination) if organic approach preferred
preventive_measures: Regular leaf removal — remove dry/diseased leaves at base every 3-4 weeks
Alternate fungicides to prevent resistance: Mancozeb → Chlorothalonil → Propiconazole
Maintain row spacing for air circulation (1.8 × 1.8 m minimum)
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
do_not: Spray in same direction as wind — fungicide won't reach leaf undersides
Leave removed infected leaves in or near the field
Use only one fungicide repeatedly — builds resistance
watch_for: Progression from leaf streaks to large dead leaf areas (indicates worsening)
Bunch filling poorly despite healthy-looking plant
Shrivelled or prematurely yellowing fingers on bunch
Sigatoka (Yellow Sigatoka / Black Sigato.timeline: With treatment: new leaf infections halt in 10-14 days. Existing lesions do not reverse. Spray every 14-21 days during high-humidity monsoon.

Bunchy Top.causal_agent: Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) — transmitted by banana aphid Pentalonia nigronervosa
Bunchy Top.visual_symptoms: New leaves emerge small, narrow, stiff, with upright orientation (like a bunch at top). Dark green streaks ('dots and dashes') on midrib and petiole — best seen by holding leaf up to light. Infected plants stop growing. Affected plant never produces a bunch.
Bunchy Top.favourable_conditions: Aphid population increase in dry cool weather (November-February). Spreads through infected suckers and aphid movement.
Bunchy Top.severity_note: No cure. Infected plant must be destroyed. Can devastate entire plantations if not managed. Notifiable disease in some states.
immediate_actions: Inject infected pseudostem with Glyphosate or urea solution to kill plant quickly without regrowth
Remove and bury or burn — do NOT compost
Spray surrounding healthy plants with Imidacloprid 0.3ml/L to kill aphid vectors
Inspect all suckers from infected stool — destroy all
preventive_measures: Source suckers only from certified disease-free nurseries
Inspect all planting material for 'dots and dashes' symptom before planting
Control aphid population: spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL 0.5ml/L every 3 weeks in dry season
Remove infected volunteers and wild banana plants near farm
do_not: Take suckers from any plant that showed BBTV symptoms
Leave infected plants standing — aphids will spread virus
watch_for: Dots and dashes pattern on midrib (diagnostic sign)
Plants not producing any new leaves
Bunchy Top.timeline: Infected plant must be killed within 1 week of detection. Monitor for new infections for 4-6 weeks.

Rhizome Rot / Corm Rot.visual_symptoms: Plant suddenly collapses without prior wilting. Pseudostem falls at base. Corm (underground stem) shows soft, rotten, foul-smelling tissue when dug up. Roots blackened.
Rhizome Rot / Corm Rot.favourable_conditions: Waterlogged soils, poor drainage, soil temperature >30°C. Often follows mechanical damage to corm from tools or rodents.
Rhizome Rot / Corm Rot.severity_note: Kills plant rapidly. Spread through soil water movement.
immediate_actions: Improve drainage immediately — break any hardpan layer if present
Drench surrounding soil with Copper Oxychloride 0.3% or Metalaxyl-M
Remove and destroy infected corms
Avoid waterlogging in irrigation schedule
preventive_measures: Plant on raised beds or ridges in heavy-rainfall areas
Do not injure corm during intercultural operations
Drench corm at planting with Trichoderma viride 2g/L
do_not: Over-irrigate — especially avoid basin flooding method
Leave water stagnant around pseudostem base
watch_for: Sudden tilting or collapse of pseudostem
Rhizome Rot / Corm Rot.timeline: Affected plant cannot be saved. Adjacent plants can be protected with drainage improvement and fungicide drench.

Banana Stem Weevil.visual_symptoms: Reddish-brown exudate (sap) oozing from pseudostem. Tunnels visible when pseudostem is split. Plant growth slows, leaves wilt. Gummy frass at base.
immediate_actions: Inject Chlorpyrifos 2.5ml/L into bore holes using syringe
Apply Carbofuran 3G granules 25g/plant at pseudostem base
Plug bore holes with moist soil after injection
preventive_measures: Remove and destroy dry leaf sheaths where adults shelter
Set trap: cut pseudostem pieces smeared with Chlorpyrifos at field borders
do_not: Leave dry sheaths attached to pseudostem

Banana Aphid.visual_symptoms: Small brown aphids clustered on inner leaf sheaths and suckers. BBTV virus vector — more dangerous than direct feeding damage.
immediate_actions: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL 0.3ml/L or Dimethoate 30 EC 2ml/L
Target inner leaf sheaths where aphids hide
preventive_measures: Regular inspection of inner sheaths monthly
Remove excess suckers — reduces aphid habitat
do_not: Ignore aphids even at low populations — BBTV risk is severe

fertilizer_schedule.note: Per plant for G9 variety (12-month crop)
fertilizer_schedule.at_planting: FYM 10 kg + Neem cake 250g per pit
fertilizer_schedule.3_to_6_months: Urea 100g + MOP 100g monthly (grand growth phase — critical for bunch size)
fertilizer_schedule.flowering: MOP 150g extra at flower emergence — improves finger filling
fertilizer_schedule.note_k: Banana is highly potassium-demanding. Deficiency causes 'T' shaped leaf and poor bunch weight.

irrigation.water_requirement_liters_per_day: 8-12 litres per plant in summer, 5-7 in winter
irrigation.drip_recommendation: Drip at 8 LPH emitter, 2 emitters per plant. Critical for water use efficiency in Solapur belt.

harvesting.maturity_indicators: Fingers become rounded (angular ridges fill out), skin turns light green-yellow, 75-80 days after bunch emergence
harvesting.post_harvest: Harvest early morning. Handle gently — bruising causes premature ripening. Store at 13-14°C for transport.
